checkpoints.reasoning: Introductions supply personalities and broad tensions, but no murder evidence distinguishes anyone.
Artie faces dismissal; several others face financial or artistic injury. Poison bottle and private toast favor staff with intake or service access, but no act connects them yet.
Death follows the toast, consistent with poison. Unaccepted terms preserve motive to stop the gift but weaken any assumption that threatened changes had already occurred.

Everyone now has a personal grievance or threatened exposure. Hugh faces fraud exposure and Artie dismissal; service staff have opportunity. Monet and Anne need funding, making killing less clearly useful.

Individual glass poisoning and concealed bottle breach make collection handling and unattended-place access central. Staff could connect both routes, but service testimony alone does not establish who adulterated the glass.

Brie supplies flavoring directly to the glass; Anya has cupboard access; Hugh knows original contents and suppressed the sale terms. Tess, Anne, Dada, Barb and Minnie admit unattended-place access. Artie and Sue are occupied at a public desk, but timing is not yet tight enough to clear them.

Evidence establishes actual poison bottle, open access, bare glass, and real consumed toast. Clean flavoring container still leaves Brie able to add poison separately. Red-band scrap ties bottle handling to glass but lacks a unique match. Staff keys and staff contents query leave multiple plausible informed suspects; many peripheral disputes have documented settlements.

Anne now insists her only visit was with the tour at the private place. The completed docent note explicitly excludes donor room and place; her earlier admission describes staying at the table. This distinctive false alibi outweighs remaining access suspicions.

final_feedback.fairness: The route contradiction is explicit and uses available evidence, so accusation is fair. Means is supported by staff access and contents warning, though neither uniquely assigns bottle opening to Anne.

remaining_plausible_alternatives.name: Brie DeVivre
remaining_plausible_alternatives.why: Directly dosed the individual glass; a clean retained ingredient does not rule out adding cyanide separately.

remaining_plausible_alternatives.name: Anya Tique
remaining_plausible_alternatives.why: Admits visiting the cupboard with a working spare key while the bottle was inside.

remaining_plausible_alternatives.name: Barb Dwyer
remaining_plausible_alternatives.why: Deliberately destroyed recording opportunity and visited the prepared unattended place; access remains plausible.

final_feedback.contrivance: Many dossiers methodically resolve one possible misleading interpretation each. Anne uniquely makes an easily checked denial late, which feels like a planted final tell; school motive is humane but escalation to murder remains thin.
final_feedback.voice: Personal relationships and mundane coping make voices substantially more alive. Repeated admissions followed by named interpersonal asides create a noticeable shared speech rhythm.
final_feedback.final_speeches_interpret_puzzle: Yes. Most explicitly restate documentary resolutions (physical bottle, real toast, power removal, no substitution, clean ingredient); Anne supplies the standout contradiction. This makes elimination highly guided even without a narrator explaining the solution.

post_vote_feedback: Confession confirms my accusation and the exact false-tour-alibi inference. It adds no necessary late proof of identity, though it asserts bottle use that access evidence only made possible. Endings give humane relational consequences but share a repeated denial/evidence/ethical admission/addressed-person structure. Anne motive remains less convincing than her detection: a threatened educational promise does not by itself dramatize why murder became her choice.
